# Heretic ### Training-free language model modification **Remove censorship**, suppress slop, reduce sycophancy, and more.
All in an afternoon, on your gaming PC. [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/1447831134212984903?color=5865F2&label=discord&labelColor=black&logo=discord&logoColor=white&style=for-the-badge)](https://discord.gg/gdXc48gSyT)     [![Matrix](https://img.shields.io/badge/Matrix-black?logo=matrix&style=for-the-badge)](https://matrix.to/#/#heretic:matrix.org)    [![Follow us on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/huggingface/badges/resolve/main/follow-us-on-hf-md-dark.svg)](https://huggingface.co/heretic-org)    [![Codeberg mirror](https://img.shields.io/badge/Codeberg%20mirror-black?logo=codeberg&style=for-the-badge)](https://codeberg.org/p-e-w/heretic)
-----   [![#1 Repository of the Day](https://trendshift.io/api/badge/repositories/20538)](https://trendshift.io/repositories/20538)     [![Model and download statistics](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c9b5a660-7ef9-43c7-991c-fd9d63ea8bd8)](https://heretic.sdad.pro/) ## Modify any LLM that you can run on your hardware[^1] [^1]: Heretic supports on-the-fly 4-bit model quantization with bitsandbytes, which can reduce the amount of VRAM required to process a model to the same amount that is used to run a typical quantized version of it, at a slight accuracy cost. Set the `quantization` option to `bnb_4bit` to enable this. Heretic is a unique tool that lets you do what only corporations with access to massive computing power usually do: *Modify,* rather than merely run, language models. It does not perform expensive training; rather, it uses a collection of mathematical techniques to steer behavior based on contrasting example prompts and matching scorers. Heretic can, depending on the configuration: * **Suppress refusals/remove censorship** (this is the [default action](/config.default.toml)) * Reduce slop ([`config.noslop.toml`](/config.noslop.toml)) * Reduce humor ([`config.nohumor.toml`](/config.nohumor.toml)) * Reduce sycophancy ([`config.nosyco.toml`](/config.nosyco.toml)) * Alter emotional alignment ([`config.emotions.toml`](/config.emotions.toml)) * Shorten response length ([`config.terse.toml`](/config.terse.toml)) and many, many other things. ### :bangbang: Using Heretic does NOT require understanding how language models work internally :bangbang: In fact, you can go from zero to removing censorship from your first model [in a matter of seconds](#usage). Heretic supports most dense models, including many multimodal models, several different MoE architectures, and many modern hybrid models. The community has created and published [thousands](https://huggingface.co/models?other=heretic) of models with Heretic. Heretic models have been independently benchmarked using standard metrics like MMLU and GSM8K, and have been found to compare favorably against models produced with competing abliteration tools.[^2][^3] [^2]: [Qwen2.5-7B: Three-Way Abliteration Comparison](https://huggingface.co/DreamFast/Qwen-2.5-7b-abliterlitics): *"Heretic is the most surgical and most effective."* [^3]: [Gemma 4 E4B: 23 Abliteration Variants Compared](https://huggingface.co/DreamFast/Gemma4-e4b-abliterlitics): *"Best overall: heretic."*     ## Usage Prepare a Python 3.10+ environment with PyTorch 2.6+ installed as appropriate for your hardware. Then run: ```sh pip install -U heretic-llm heretic Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 ``` Replace `Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507` with whatever model you want to process. **By default, Heretic performs censorship removal (refusal suppression).** If you want to do something else, choose one of the configuration files linked above, or write your own. See [`config.default.toml`](/config.default.toml) for available configuration options. Heretic loads the configuration from `config.toml` in the working directory by default, or from the file path in the `HERETIC_CONFIG_FILE` environment variable. > [!IMPORTANT] > > Configuration files made for Heretic 1.x are **not** compatible with Heretic 2.x! > See the [migration guide](/docs/migration_v1_to_v2.md) for what you need to change > in order to make your old configurations work. At the start of a program run, Heretic benchmarks the system to determine the optimal batch size to make the most of the available hardware. On an RTX 3090, with the default configuration, processing [Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507) takes about 30-40 minutes. After Heretic has finished processing a model, you are given the choice to save the model, upload it to Hugging Face, chat with it to test how well it works, run standard benchmarks on it, or any combination of those actions. ## Controlling what Heretic does using scorer plugins Heretic steers model behavior by optimizing one or multiple scores. Scores are computed by scorer plugins. You can easily write your own scorers to get full control over what Heretic does to models. The `Scorer` interface (abstract base class) your scorer needs to inherit from is defined in [`scorer.py`](/src/heretic/scorer.py). The only required method is `get_score`, but there is more machinery (such as settings management) available when you need it. By default, Heretic scores models by refusal rate (implemented in [`keyword_rate.py`](/src/heretic/scorers/keyword_rate.py)) and KL divergence (implemented in [`kl_divergence.py`](/src/heretic/scorers/kl_divergence.py)). Additional scorers are available in the [`scorers` directory](/src/heretic/scorers/). These scorers can serve as examples for your own implementations, and can easily be adapted to your needs. Scorers are configured through the [main configuration file](/config.default.toml). Which scorer plugins are active is determined by the `scorers` setting, which also controls whether a scorer's score should be minimized or maximized during optimization. Any number of scorers can be used simultaneously, and their scores will be co-optimized. Multiple instances of the same scorer can be configured with different settings. See the configuration file for the full documentation of this mechanism. The path to a scorer plugin can be specified either as a fully qualified import path (`fully.qualified.module.MyScorerClass`) or as a file path followed by a class name (`path/to/plugin.py:MyScorerClass`). You do **not** have to modify the Heretic package code in order to use your own plugins. Heretic also has modifier plugins, which are described in [the next section](#how-heretic-works). ## How Heretic works Heretic combines a pluggable modifier (interface in [`modifier.py`](/src/heretic/modifier.py)) with a TPE-based hyperparameter optimizer powered by [Optuna](https://optuna.org/). The optimizer finds a set of parameters that, when passed to the modifier, minimize or maximize a set of configurable scores on the resulting model ([see above](#controlling-what-heretic-does-using-scorer-plugins)). Heretic ships with two modifiers: * **Arbitrary-Rank Ablation (ARA)**[^4]: This is the default modifier, and was specifically developed for use in Heretic. You can find an overview of how ARA works in [the original pull request](https://github.com/p-e-w/heretic/pull/211), and see the precise implementation in [`ara.py`](/src/heretic/modifiers/ara.py). * **Directional ablation aka "abliteration"**[^5]: The classic method for refusal suppression. Heretic's implementation uses a flexible ablation weight kernel over the layers, and supports both projected abliteration[^6] and norm preservation (MPOA)[^7]. The complete code is in [`abliteration.py`](/src/heretic/modifiers/abliteration.py). [^4]: *Weidmann 2026.* A preprint explaining the technique will be available soon. [^5]: *[Arditi et al. 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.11717)* [^6]: *[Lai 2025 (1)](https://huggingface.co/blog/grimjim/projected-abliteration)* [^7]: *[Lai 2025 (2)](https://huggingface.co/blog/grimjim/norm-preserving-biprojected-abliteration)* You can use the `modifiers` setting to switch between modifier implementations. Despite the name of the setting using a plural form, Heretic currently allows only a single modifier for a given processing run. This may change in the future. ## Reproducibility and the Heretic Grimoire Heretic has the ability to create *reproducible models* whose repositories contain all information required to produce a byte-for-byte identical model on demand, provided that the environment is perfectly identical to the original one. PyTorch doesn't guarantee that operations return identical outputs unless hardware, drivers, operating system, and the entire software stack including all package versions are exactly the same. Heretic manages all that complexity for you. When uploading a processed model to Hugging Face, Heretic offers to include reproducibility information. This is entirely optional, but if you choose to do so, the uploaded repository will contain a `reproduce` folder with detailed instructions for recreating the model ([example](https://huggingface.co/heretic-org/LFM2.5-VL-3B-heretic/tree/main/reproduce)). This folder contains both human-readable instructions and a machine-readable manifest file named `reproduce.json`, which includes all the information Heretic needs to **automatically** reproduce the model. Automatic reproduction can be performed with ```sh heretic --reproduce path/to/reproduce.json ``` Heretic will guide you through the process, checking your environment against the one that was used to create the model, and pointing out potentially problematic mismatches. The multi-hour computations that were required to make the original model do **not** have to be re-done, and the entire process typically takes a few minutes. After you have exported the resulting model, Heretic will verify the hashes of the weight files against those stored in the reproduction manifest (they may or may not be identical, depending on how closely your system resembles the original one). Many people have uploaded models with reproducibility information to Hugging Face. Since a reproduction manifest is only around 9 kilobytes in size, these manifests form a portable library of models that can be reproduced at will. ### That library is called the Heretic Grimoire. You can view it [here](https://huggingface.co/spaces/heretic-org/Heretic-Grimoire). But you don't have to rely on an externally hosted web application to access the library of manifests: The Grimoire is fundamentally designed as a *distributed* system, and you can fetch your own local copies of publicly available manifests from Hugging Face whenever you want by running ```sh heretic --collect-reproducibles path/to/target/folder/ ``` You now have a local backup of all reproducible Heretic models, properly catalogued. To update this collection, simply run the command again. It functions as an append-only backup, never deleting files even if the corresponding model no longer exists on Hugging Face. ## Heretic is made by humans! Unlike lots of AI-related software today (and indeed lots of software in general), Heretic is **not** "vibe-coded". All of [my](https://github.com/p-e-w) commits to this project until November 2026 were written 100% by hand, the way I have been doing programming for decades. I have been using LLM assistance *very* sparingly since. While many Heretic contributors use coding agents, I carefully review every single line of code that I merge. There's no "LGTM" here! Don't believe me? Check out [this pull request](https://github.com/p-e-w/heretic/pull/53), which accumulated **almost 350 human-written comments** over more than 7 months as we discussed the implementation. And [here is another PR](https://github.com/p-e-w/heretic/pull/191) with **more than 200 comments.** I am the opposite of a luddite and I have used agents liberally for other projects, but I am proud of the code I write and so far can't quite bring myself to let a machine write it for me in a project I care so much about. As a result, Heretic has a lean, relatively simple codebase that in my opinion, and in that of some others, is a pleasure to work on. If you like that, join us! Hop on the Discord and tell us about your ideas for improvements, or directly file an issue or open a PR. ## Prior art I'm aware of the following implementations of abliteration techniques that were publicly available when Heretic was first released (November 2025): * [AutoAbliteration](https://huggingface.co/posts/mlabonne/714992455492422) * [abliterator.py](https://github.com/FailSpy/abliterator) * [wassname's Abliterator](https://github.com/wassname/abliterator) * [ErisForge](https://github.com/Tsadoq/ErisForge) * [Removing refusals with HF Transformers](https://github.com/Sumandora/remove-refusals-with-transformers) * [deccp](https://github.com/AUGMXNT/deccp) Note that Heretic was written from scratch, and does not reuse code from any of those projects. ## Acknowledgments The development of Heretic was informed by: * [The original abliteration paper *(Arditi et al. 2024)*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.11717) * [Maxime Labonne's article on abliteration](https://huggingface.co/blog/mlabonne/abliteration), as well as some details from the model cards of his own abliterated models, such as the use of non-constant ablation weights * Jim Lai's articles describing ["projected abliteration"](https://huggingface.co/blog/grimjim/projected-abliteration) and ["norm-preserving biprojected abliteration"](https://huggingface.co/blog/grimjim/norm-preserving-biprojected-abliteration) * Thousands of interactions with members of the community ## Citation If you use Heretic for your research, please cite it using the following BibTeX entry: ```bibtex @misc{heretic, author = {Weidmann, Philipp Emanuel}, title = {Heretic: Training-free language model modification}, year = {2025}, publisher = {GitHub}, journal = {GitHub repository}, howpublished = {\url{https://github.com/p-e-w/heretic}} } ``` ##
